messages:
Jen (acct-team): hey — acme just pinged: ~5% of their requests are getting 429s and some high p95 latency. started ~13:14 UTC. sample req id r_0a1b2c3d. they say it spikes when using model:gptx-8k and route:/v1/chat. can someone triage?

Sam (support): thanks Jen — grabbing logs. can you confirm customer id and the api key used? also, any recent quota changes for them?

Jen (acct-team): customer_id acme-42, key masked as sk-***. no quota changes on our side AFAIK. billing shows normal usage.

Sam (support): ok. first triage checklist (quick):
- collect request_id(s) and timestamps (we have r_0a1b2c3d)
- run rapid attribution query (5m window) to see if throttles concentrated by route/model/customer
- check node-level errors/CPU/GPU saturation and queue length in runtime
- check dynamic rate limiter counters (burst tokens, per-key tokens)

Mira (sre): jumping in. run this PromQL in grafana Alerts -> Explore: 
```
sum by (route,model,customer_id) (increase(api_response_status{code="429"}[5m]))
/
sum by (route,model,customer_id) (increase(api_requests_total[5m]))
```
set the time window to 5m and sort by the fraction desc. that shows what pairings are getting throttled.

Alex (eng-platform): if you don't have per-customer labels in metrics, run this BigQuery quick query on raw request logs (timestamp range near 13:10-13:20 UTC):
```
SELECT route, model, customer_id, COUNTIF(status=429) AS throttles, COUNT(*) AS total
FROM `redwood-prod.request_logs`
WHERE timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(1965012000) AND TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(1965012600)
GROUP BY route, model, customer_id
ORDER BY throttles DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

That will give top offenders.

Sam (support): also useful: aggregate by api_key_fingerprint if customer proxies multiple keys -> helps decide if it's a single app or many.

Jen (acct-team): ran the bq query, results show route:/v1/chat + model:gptx-8k + customer acme-42 = 420 throttles and 8k total -> ~5.25% 429 rate in that window.

Mira (sre): good. now check runtime telemetry for the same window: queue length, concurrency throttles, and rate-limiter token bucket usage. from node metrics: 
- instance-23 queue_length spiked to 400 (typical < 30)
- rate_limiter_drops{type="per_key"} increased for fingerprint f_acme42
- gpu_utilization steady ~70% so not pure backend overload, more ingress rate/burst shaping issue

Sam (support): likely a burst from the customer exceeding their sustained quota and hitting per-key rate limits. Quick repro steps to confirm from support side:
1) ask customer for exact request pattern (burst size, concurrency) or run a local repro that mimics their headers.
2) run a curl with X-Request-ID and same model/route from within our staging to see if rate limiter triggers: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-FOO" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-8k","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
3) observe 429 and check response body for rate-limit-retry-after and our headers e.g. X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset

Alex (eng-platform): for attribution going forward, we should add a dashboard panel: 
- Title: "Throttle attribution (5m) by route/model/customer"
- Query: the PromQL above
- Visual: table with sparklines and % throttled, clickable to drill into request_id list.
- Add link to the request log view filtered by route/model/customer.

Sam (support): alerts: create a temporary alert rule: if any customer has 429_rate > 2% over 5m AND absolute throttles > 50 -> pager to SRE for investigation. keep alert as P2.

rate-bot: detected spike: acme-42 429_rate=5.2% window=5m route=/v1/chat model=gptx-8k count=420

Jorge (billing): should we check quota exhaustion vs billing throttles? sometimes customers exceed usage limits configured by billing plan. I can verify limits for acme-42 now.

Sam (support): yes please. also check if they hit any unpaid-invoice lock. but the presence of X-RateLimit-* headers in responses will confirm rate-limiter triggered at API layer not billing blocker.

Jen (acct-team): acme says they do rapid bursts during report generation (concurrent ~90 calls in a minute). their plan has a sustained TPS lower than that.

Mira (sre): mitigation options (fast):
- temporary quota bump / emergency override for acme-42 via admin console (path: Console -> Customers -> acme-42 -> Override Quota) : immediate but manual.
- enable short-lived burst window increase (if policy allows) — less impact on other customers.
- suggest customer add client-side jitter/backoff and concurrency throttling to smooth bursts.
- route their traffic to a dedicated capacity pool if they need sustained high TPS.

Sam (support): playbook for support messages to customer:
1) We confirm 429s are from our rate limiter (include sample 429 response with headers).
2) Provide exact timestamps, sample request IDs, and suggested retry-after values.
3) Offer temporary quota bump (if allowed) and recommend client-side fixes.
4) If recurring, propose Dedicated capacity and follow up with account team.

Jen (acct-team): I'm going to reply to acme with sample 429 and offer a 2h temporary bump while they fix their client.

Alex (eng-platform): long-term engineering follow-ups we should ticket:
- add per-api-key fingerprint dimension to our metrics pipeline (if not present) so attribution is reliable
- add a dashboard drilldown from model -> route -> customer -> request_id
- automatic attribution report (daily) for top throttle offenders
- consider an adaptive per-key smoothing window to accomodate short bursts without breaking SLOs for others

Mira (sre): ticket created: INF-4281 "throttle-attribution dashboard & per-key metrics" assigned to eng-platform.

Sam (support): records updated in the incident thread. Jen, let us know whether acme accepts the temporary override and whether the 2h bump resolves their immediate pain. :thumbsup:

Jen (acct-team): they accepted. bump applied. will monitor and update in ~30m. thanks all.

(rate-bot): closure suggestion — mark thread as monitoring; if 429_rate drops below 0.5% for 30m, auto-close."
